ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A box of mass $m$ is at rest on a horizontal floor. The coefficients of static and kinetic friction between the box and the floor are $\mu_{0}$ and $\mu$ (where $\mu < \mu_{0}$), respectively. One end of a spring with spring constant $k$ is attached to the right side of the box, and the spring is initially at its relaxed length. The other end of the spring is pulled horizontally to the right with constant velocity $v_{0}$. As a result, the box will move in fits and starts. Assume the box does not tip over. Let $s$ be the extension of the spring when the box is just about to start moving, let $x$ be the position of the box, and let $t=0$ be the time when the box first starts moving. Define $\omega=\sqrt{k/m}$ and $r=\mu/\mu_0$.

1. Calculate the distance $s$ that the spring is stretched beyond its rest length when the box is just about to start moving.
2. Find the acceleration of the box in terms of $x$, $t$, $v_{0}$, $s$, and the other parameters, while the box is moving.
3. Find the time $t_{0}$ when the box stops for the first time.
4. After the box stops, how long will it stay at rest before starting to move again?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Take rightward as positive. Before the box moves, static friction can balance the spring force up to its maximum value μ0 m g. The box is just about to start moving when k s = μ0 m g, hence s = μ0 m g/k. For t ≥ 0 during sliding, the right end of the spring has moved an extra v0 t. If x is the displacement of the box from its position at first motion, then the spring extension is s + v0 t - x. The spring force on the box is k(s + v0 t - x) to the right, and kinetic friction is μ m g to the left. Thus m x'' = k(s + v0 t - x) - μ m g, so a = x'' = (k/m)(s + v0 t - x) - μ g. Using ω^2 = k/m and r = μ/μ0, and since k s = μ0 m g, we have μ g = r μ0 g = r k s/m = r ω^2 s. Therefore the equation of motion becomes x'' + ω^2 x = ω^2[v0 t + (1-r)s]. With x(0)=0 and x'(0)=0, the solution is x(t)=v0 t + (1-r)s(1-cos(ωt)) - (v0/ω)sin(ωt). Differentiate: x'(t)=v0(1-cos(ωt)) + (1-r)sω sin(ωt). Set x'(t)=0 for the first stop. Let θ=ωt. Then v0(1-cos θ)+(1-r)sω sin θ=0. The first nonzero root is θ=2π-2α, where α=tan^{-1}(((1-r)sω)/v0). Hence t0=(2π-2α)/ω. At this stopping instant, the spring extension is y_stop=s+v0t0-x(t0). Substituting the solution at θ=2π-2α gives y_stop=(2r-1)s. While the box is at rest, the pulled end continues moving right, increasing the extension at rate v0. The box starts moving again when the extension reaches s, so the waiting time is [s-(2r-1)s]/v0=2(1-r)s/v0.
